_README: Calibration set for tco_engine/vllm_reference PREDICTED throughput anchors.
Decode on this box is memory-bandwidth-bound, so the bytes a model reads per
token (ACTIVE parameters x bytes/param) sets the ceiling, and `efficiency` is
the measured fraction of that ceiling actually achieved.
The efficiency is DERIVED FROM THE MEASUREMENTS BELOW at import time, never
hardcoded. Every row here is a single-stream (n_users=1) figure measured on
this GB10. Do not add a row that was not measured here.
bytes_per_param is the EFFECTIVE figure (checkpoint bytes / total params),
not a nominal 0.5/1.0/2.0 -- every 2026 4-bit release is mixed-precision and
none of them is actually 0.5 B/param.

cross_hardware_validation below is THIRD-PARTY data and is deliberately NOT used to calibrate anything. It exists to BACK-TEST the cross-hardware projection (scale_throughput) against a published measurement of a model of the same class on the same rack, which is the one thing this box can never measure for itself. See scripts/smoke_tco_capacity.py::a19.

_note: DeepSeek-R1 671B-A37B is the closest published analogue to the 2026 frontier
entries: same sparse-MoE shape, same MLA attention, 37B active. These are
tok/s PER USER (interactivity) against tok/s per chip, i.e. points on a
throughput/latency Pareto curve, not a single number. A projection is
validated if it lands INSIDE the published envelope -- toward the
high-throughput end, because that is the operating point a $/MTok planner
Source states the values are interpolated from real benchmark runs, so the
envelope is the claim, not any single point.
cross_hardware_validation.source: SemiAnalysis InferenceX, DeepSeek R1 8k/1k FP4, GB200 NVL72 vs GB300 NVL72
